Synopsis:
Wyll's CRD directly after recruitment, in which you can discuss the tadpole.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_Wyll_CRD_PostRecruitment.json: This scene takes place immediately after recruiting Wyll and concerns the illithid (mind‑flayer) tadpole implanted in you both — the narrator’s “tingle” signals the tadpole reacting. Wyll, who describes himself as a veteran who once felled beasts and fiends, says the tadpole has weakened and suppressed his abilities yet he hasn’t shown the expected signs of “turning” (nausea, pain, etc.). The player’s lines show confidence or dark humor about provoking symptoms and wonder why your tadpoles haven’t produced the usual effects, suggesting your implants may be unusual. Other companions (Astarion, Shadowheart) will have their own in‑party dialogue, and later scenes (e.g., Daisy’s revelations) expand on the tadpoles’ strange magics and their role in a wider sickness.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SCO_HalsinMorningAfter.json: Halsin approaches you the morning after you celebrated your victory over the goblins. He now turns to the matter of your tadpole and how you might cure yourself - there is no quick solution, however. He tells you it'll be necessary to travel to a dangerous new region, and joins you at your camp to provide support.
- DEN_AttackOnDen_HalsinReturns.json: The Druid Grove has been saved (because either the attacking force was repelled or its leaders were assassinated) and Halsin returns. He thanks the player and reacts to events that may have transpired in the grove during his absence. He's previously promised to help the player with their tadpole problem, but he defers this discussion until the next morning after the victory celebrations.
- GLO_Tadpole_TrueSoulCorpse.json: The player witnesses an invasive parasite emerge from a dead body - the very same kind of parasite that currently resides inside them. They try to kill it, but find this curiously difficult - the little creature can psychically influence the player and tries to sway them from doing it harm. Meanwhile, Daisy encourages us to harvest it to absorb its potential.
- CAMP_DaisyMissionStatement_AvD.json: The player is already infected with a tadpole/parasite and has recently learned that these creatures are imbued with unusual magic; the dream conversation follows whatever route the player took to discover that fact. Daisy appears in a dream‑field, having returned as promised, and confronts the player about their reluctance to use the parasite’s powers or to have it removed. She explains the parasites are symptoms of a greater sickness tied to the Cult of the Absolute — the infected hear a voice and are being groomed to worship it — and warns the cult is winning a hidden war that would doom Faerûn if unchecked. Daisy urges the player to join her plan to infiltrate and undermine the Absolute using their tadpole powers, and at the dream’s end she grants the player a new tadpole ability.

Halsin approaches you the morning after you celebrated your victory over the goblins. He now turns to the matter of your tadpole and how you might cure yourself - there is no quick solution, however. He tells you it'll be necessary to travel to a dangerous new region, and joins you at your camp to provide support.

The Druid Grove has been saved (because either the attacking force was repelled or its leaders were assassinated) and Halsin returns. He thanks the player and reacts to events that may have transpired in the grove during his absence. He's previously promised to help the player with their tadpole problem, but he defers this discussion until the next morning after the victory celebrations.

The player witnesses an invasive parasite emerge from a dead body - the very same kind of parasite that currently resides inside them. They try to kill it, but find this curiously difficult - the little creature can psychically influence the player and tries to sway them from doing it harm. Meanwhile, Daisy encourages us to harvest it to absorb its potential.

context: You and Wyll are at camp immediately after recruiting him; a sudden mental tingle signals the illithid tadpoles inside both of you reacting. Wyll — a self‑described veteran who says he’s felled beasts and fiends — explains the tadpole has weakened and suppressed some of his abilities, yet he hasn’t shown the expected “turning” symptoms (nausea, pain, etc.). The player also bears a tadpole and responds with confidence or dark humor, wondering why the usual effects haven’t appeared and suggesting your implants may be unusual. Other companions and later scenes will expand on the tadpoles’ strange magics and their link to a wider sickness, but this scene is primarily an initial check‑in about the implants and Wyll’s bafflement.
